report_name: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack Harvests Credentials from 2,500 Firms

threat_actors.name: Team PCP
threat_actors.description: A threat group that conducted a major supply chain attack against the LiteLLM open-source AI framework by publishing malicious versions to PyPI. The group's objective was to harvest cloud credentials, API keys, and other secrets from AI development environments.
threat_actors.goals: To harvest sensitive credentials, including cloud provider credentials and API keys for services like OpenAI, Azure, and Google Vertex AI, from AI development and CI/CD environments.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: Team PCP published malicious versions (1.82.7 and 1.82.8) of the LiteLLM package to the official PyPI repository, compromising the software supply chain for its users.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: The malicious code within the trojanized LiteLLM package was designed to scan the environment and steal credentials stored in files and configuration management systems.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: Harvested secrets, including API keys, SSH keys, and cloud credentials, were exfiltrated from compromised environments to an external server controlled by Team PCP.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: The malicious package used .pth files to execute arbitrary Python code. These files are automatically processed by the Python interpreter upon startup, providing a stealthy execution and persistence mechanism.

malware.name: Malicious LiteLLM Package
malware.description: Trojanized versions (1.82.7 and 1.82.8) of the LiteLLM Python package published to PyPI. The malware scans for credentials in files and environment variables and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled server using stealthy execution via .pth files.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: A popular open-source Python package that acts as a universal interface for LLM APIs. It was compromised and trojanized by Team PCP in a supply chain attack.

tools.name: Trivy
tools.description: A development tool from Aqua Security that was compromised by Team PCP to obtain initial credentials for escalating access to publish malicious packages.

identities.name: Over 2,500 companies
identities.description: A class of over 2,500 organizations and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines exposed to credential theft due to installing malicious versions of the LiteLLM package.

identities.name: PyPI
identities.description: The Python Package Index (PyPI) was the distribution platform abused by Team PCP to publish the malicious LiteLLM packages.

infrastructure.name: Team PCP Exfiltration Server
infrastructure.description: An attacker-controlled server used to receive credentials and other secrets harvested by the malicious LiteLLM packages.

indicators.name: Installation of Malicious LiteLLM Package
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Installation of Malicious LiteLLM Package
id: 7c5b1a3d-8f9e-4b1c-9d2e-1a2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects the installation of malicious versions (1.82.7, 1.82.8) of the LiteLLM Python package via pip or other package managers.
references:
  - https://www.cloudsek.com/blog/ai-supply-chain-breach-2500-companies-434000-cicd-pipelines
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-11
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.initial_access
level: critical
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'litellm==1.82.7'
      - 'litellm==1.82.8'
  filter_legit:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'uninstall'
      - 'pip-audit'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
indicators.description: Detects command-line execution for the installation of the specific malicious versions of the LiteLLM package.

indicators.name: Suspicious Python .pth File Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Python .pth File Modification
id: 8d9e2f3a-1b2c-4d5e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: 'Detects the creation or modification of .pth files by unexpected processes. The LiteLLM supply chain attack used .pth files for stealthy code execution.'
references:
  - https://www.cloudsek.com/blog/ai-supply-chain-breach-2500-companies-434000-cicd-pipelines
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-11
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.execution
  - attack.persistence
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_pth:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.pth'
  filter_legit_procs:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\pip.exe'
      - '\pip3.exe'
  condition: selection_pth and not filter_legit_procs
indicators.description: Detects the creation or modification of Python .pth files by processes other than standard Python installers, a technique used for stealthy execution in the LiteLLM attack.

indicators.name: Anomalous Outbound Traffic from Python Process
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Outbound Traffic from Python Process
id: 9e0f1a2b-3c4d-5e6f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b
status: experimental
description: 'Detects unusual outbound network traffic from Python processes, which could indicate data exfiltration by a malicious package like the one in the LiteLLM attack. This rule should be tuned by adding known-good domains to the filter.'
references:
  - https://www.cloudsek.com/blog/ai-supply-chain-breach-2500-companies-434000-cicd-pipelines
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-11
tags:
  - attack.t1048
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\python.exe'
    Initiated: true
  filter_known_good:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - '.python.org'
      - 'pypi.org'
      - '.windows.net'
      - '.microsoft.com'
      - '.google.com'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_good
indicators.description: Detects potentially anomalous outbound network connections from Python processes, which could be indicative of credential exfiltration by a compromised package.

relationships.target_name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Outbound Traffic from Python Process
